Priya Rao: FYI we're seeing a sudden egress throttle to ap-south1 (11:45 UTC). GPU pod allocs are piling up, queue depth spiking, and a subset of requests are getting rejected. I've kicked a partial diversion to eu-west to keep latencies bounded; cost is spiking. Need a quick post-incident runbook update and a safer traffic-shift strategy.
Samir Patel: On it. Can you paste the short logs and the command you used to shift?
Priya Rao: logs: `alloc_wait_ms=4200, queue_len=187, pod_retries=12, egress_err=ECONNRESET`
Priya Rao: shift command I ran (manual):
```
# emergency soft shift 20%
redwood traffic shift --from ap-south1 --to eu-west --percent 20 --mode soft --reason "egress-throttle, keep tails low"
```
Samir Patel: Thanks. Two quick notes: (1) the ACL change looks like an external peering policy change — network team alerted infra at 11:40 UTC, (2) current runbook only has hard-weighted shifts which causes big capacity oscillations.
Jon Lee: Agree with Samir. Suggest adding a circuit-breaker + progressive ramp (soft-shift) with guardrails: max_drain_per_min, rollback_on_error=true, and cost_budget check.
Grace Miller: Also we should add a pre-shift verification that checks warm-pool fill in target region and that target_sla_pct >= 98.
Eve Johnson: I can own the runbook edits. Proposed new steps:
  - detect: threshold queue_len>100 or alloc_wait_ms>2000 -> page oncall
  - mitigate: run soft-shift (20% -> 50% step increments every 5m)
  - validate: check target region pod readiness, request latency, and token-cost delta
  - rollback: automated rollback if error_rate increases >1.5x or cost delta > +40% in 30m
Samir Patel: We should also add a small canary that routes non-critical traffic (dev keys) first. Lower blast radius.
Priya Rao: Good. Also logging: include `egress_peer_id` and `bgp_path_change` in incident packet. Those helped root-cause here.
infra-bot: Created incident INC-20234 and attached initial alert timeline (https://redwood.incidents/INC-20234) :white_check_mark:
Jon Lee: Action items from thread:
  - Eve: update runbook markdown with soft-shift steps and verification checklist (PR target EOD)
  - Grace: add warm-pool pre-check endpoint + docs (PR next week)
  - Samir: add network detection rules for egress ACL/BGP path changes (ticket NW-548)
  - Priya: follow up with accounting on cost spike and add cost_budget guard to shift tool
  - infra-bot: emit `shift_preview` message on dry-run to #eng-runtime when someone runs dry-run
Grace Miller: Small implementation tip: `max_drain_per_min` needs to be region-aware (different target capacities). Also expose `soft_shift_step_ms` so we can tune ramp speed.
Priya Rao: I'll run a controlled dry-run this afternoon (13:30 UTC) and post the results. Please subscribe to INC-20234.
Samir Patel: If anyone's free, pair with me on the shift tool change; want to add `--cost-budget` flag to `redwood traffic shift`.
Eve Johnson: acked. I'll open the PR and link it to INC-20234.
infra-bot: Runbook file updated: /runbooks/egress_throttle_soft_shift.md (draft) — PR #1294 opened by Eve Johnson
Priya Rao: thanks all. Postmortem note: make sure the runbook highlights "don't hard-shift >30% without warm-pool check". This incident would have been worse without the quick partial soft-shift. :sparkles:
